messages:
elena: heads-up: ticket #7894 — multiple HK customers report high latency (200-600ms), intermittent 502s and auth 401s. They say traffic is landing in us-east and billing shows sudden egress. attaching quick repro outputs below.

elena: ```
$ dig +short @203.90.10.5 inference.redwood-inference.com
52.23.145.12
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.redwood-inference.com
13.225.43.77

# curl -sI -H 'Host: inference.redwood-inference.com' http://52.23.145.12 | egrep -i 'x-edge-pop|x-request-id'
X-Edge-Pop: us-east1
X-Request-Id: r-0a1b2c3d
```

elena: customer: ISP is "PacificNet HK" (resolver seen: 203.90.10.5). They started seeing this ~0320 UTC, TTLs look long on their side. Billing spike for cross-region egress noted.

jordan: thanks. initial hypothesis: resolver or ISP cache returning us-east answer because EDNS-client-subnet removed / ISP prefetched a stale cached A. can you confirm whether the edge geodb sync job reported any issues?

elena: i checked console metrics — edge geodb shows last sync 2025-11-12 03:12 UTC (job failed once then retried), but that shouldn't cause per-resolver misroutes for long.

samir: two possibilities: 1) upstream resolver is stripping ECS so authoritative sees no client location and falls back to default us-east answer; 2) ISP NAT/resolver cache is sticky with long TTL. both can cause hk->us routing. can we get a packet-level repro from the customer (dig +trace) and an HTTP trace showing X-Forwarded-For?

elena: sent steps to customer: 1) dig +trace inference.redwood-inference.com @203.90.10.5 2) curl -v --resolve inference.redwood-inference.com:443:52.23.145.12 https://inference.redwood-inference.com/v1/models | sed -n '1,20p'

elena: customer pasted results: dig +trace shows their resolver returned 52.23.145.12 from cache; trace shows no EDNS client subnet opt.

jordan: can we confirm authoritative name server logs? if our authoritative sees queries without ECS and then our geo-fallback policy pins to us-east, that's expected behavior. also need to check our DNS TTLs and whether we recently rotated any CNAMEs that changed geo-answers.

samir: checking auth logs now...
samir: (quick scan) queries from 203.90.10.5 -> no ECS, answered with us-east pool because default region fallback policy kicks in when ECS absent + model variant affinity.

netops-bot: geodb-sync job failed: task geodb-sync-20251112 exited nonzero (code 2). next retry scheduled in 15m.\\noncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-7894 -> "HK customers routed to US-east due to resolver cache / missing ECS". Pager duty alerted.

leo: short-term mitigation: we can 1) lower DNS answer TTL for inference.redwood-inference.com to 30s for rollout, 2) add a heuristic to prefer APAC pool when ASN/resolver in our ASN->region mapping includes known APAC ISPs even if ECS missing, or 3) issue CDN geoip purge. which is fastest?

jordan: 1) TTL change is fastest. 2) but note some resolvers will ignore new TTL until their cache expires. still worth doing. 3) purge geodb on edge proxies after confirming sync.

elena: applied TTL=30s on staging nameserver; pushing to prod now (will update once DNS changes propagate). told customer to flush local resolver cache and test after 30s.

samir: i'm opening a vendor ticket with our CDN partner — include sample resolver IP 203.90.10.5, timing, and traceroute showing path lands in us-east. request: check if their edge geodb mapping for that resolver ASN is incorrectly labeled as north-america.

samir: also created a short-term routing rule: if resolver IP ASN in our known APAC list and ECS absent, route to apac pool. rolling this to canary in 2 hosts.

elena: customer tried curl after ~2m: still got us-east. they ran "dig +short @203.90.10.5 inference.redwood-inference.com" and got same us-east IP. they say ISP cache TTL ~24h.

jordan: that's the tricky bit — ISP-level resolver cache. even with our TTL change, upstream cache persists until they expire. we should 1) prioritize route override for requests with X-Forwarded-For ASN that maps to HK, 2) request CDN vendor to serve stale answer with local pop header so we can detect misroutes in metrics.

leo: agree. i'll patch the routing override to prefer apac for incoming connections where the client IP ASN maps to APAC (this uses L3 info not ECS). deploy to canary now.

netops-bot: routing override canary deployed to canary-1 and canary-2 (2 hosts).

elena: customer reports improved latency after ~6m and auth 401s stopped. billing team asked for estimate of excess egress to offset charges.

samir: preliminary calc: affected customers ~7 accounts, average additional egress ~12GB each in 40m window -> estimate extra cost ~ $0.85 * 7 * 12 ≈ $71 for that window (very rough). forwarding to billing for credit evaluation.

jordan: follow-ups: - CDN vendor ticket #CDN-4556 (assigned) - add resolver-IP -> ASN mapping to our monitoring to catch this earlier - long-term: re-evaluate fallback policy when ECS missing (maybe honor ASN->region mapping first)

elena: will update the support ticket and let customers know mitigation + billing escalation. thanks all. :thumbsup:

leo: note: schedule forced geodb re-sync and a manual sanity check across regions.

elena: closing loop here; will post a short postmortem once vendor reply confirmed.
